facts: Group a contains TWO circuits, not one.
Left circuit has two battery cells in the left branch, a capacitor in the middle branch, and an inductor in the right branch.
Switch pivot is connected to the capacitor upper plate; blade touches contact 1 toward the battery and not contact 2 toward the inductor.
All three lower branch ends share a return conductor.
Capacitor upper plate bears positive signs and q_m; lower plate bears negative signs and -q_m.
Contacts are labelled 1 and 2. No current arrow is present.
Right circuit repeats the two-cell battery, capacitor and inductor.
Switch blade touches contact 2 toward the inductor; battery contact 1 is visibly disconnected.
The capacitor is still positive q_m on top and negative -q_m below in this initial switched state.
The capacitor and inductor form a closed loop through their common bottom return; battery positive branch is open.
No current arrow is present.
A single vertical spring hangs from a fixed hatched horizontal support and carries one mass.
A horizontal dash-dot equilibrium guide runs through the spring's lower junction above the mass center.
The mass center lies BELOW the equilibrium line, depicting positive downward displacement from equilibrium.
A separate solid horizontal line from the mass center and a vertical dimension mark show the separation from equilibrium, labelled x_m.
Source equilibrium words and a/b grouping marks are annotations, not extra apparatus.

notes: Canonical PNG and two existing source spring crops were inspected before comparing modern spec/SVG. All SIX electrical states and BOTH spring pictures are retained.

Source electrical rows contain three states each: first quarter starts with +q_m/-q_m, passes through +q/-q with downward i, and ends with blank plates/downward I_m. Second quarter starts by repeating blank plates/downward I_m, passes through -q/+q with downward i, and ends with -q_m/+q_m and no current arrow.
Exactly four current arrows point down beside the right-hand coils; none reverses within this depicted half-period. No current arrow is added to either maximum-charge endpoint.

The source top spring mass lies on the broken equilibrium guide and has vector-accent v_m, NOT v_x. Its horizontal position extension is unarrowed; the vector accent over v is not a horizontal mass-motion arrow.
The source bottom spring mass is ABOVE the equilibrium guide, with a shorter spring, source vector-accent x_m, solid position extension and unarrowed vertical displacement marker.
The source first/second quarter captions are translated, not reinterpreted as first/second full periods.

The six panels show one half-period: electrical energy initially maximal/current zero, then magnetic energy maximal/charge zero at T/4, then opposite electrical polarity/current zero at T/2. Reversed charge is not a full-period return. Complete N18 ZH/EN explicitly explains that a full period restores both charge polarity and current direction.
The duplicated neutral state is the shared T/4 boundary between the two source quarter-period rows, not a missing or extra quarter of the cycle.

Downward coil current is consistent with discharging the initially positive top plate and then charging it negatively. Current magnitude increases toward I_m in the first quarter and decreases without reversal in the second quarter.

Complete N19 ZH/EN maps velocity/current and spring/electromagnetic energies. The top spring has zero displacement and maximum speed; the second is at the opposite displacement extremum and zero speed. Source x_m denotes maximum displacement magnitude, not a fabricated positive signed coordinate at both extrema.
N19 prose v_x is the velocity component; the source spring label v_m denotes its maximum magnitude. Replacing the drawing label with v_x would lose source meaning.

The N19 derivative i=q' concerns transferred charge in the chosen current direction, not necessarily the charge on the initially upper positive capacitor plate; downward arrows do not require a false positive derivative of that decreasing plate charge.

All 101 semantic segments/arrows have connects assertions. Each current arrow additionally has displacement dx=0, dy=-106. Spring mass/reference assertions are dy=0 for equilibrium and dy=+50 for the mass above equilibrium. Marker span is 50 drawing units. No source grid or labelled point constellation is omitted.

Viewed the complete existing 640x1040 preview and existing 331px mobile scroll-end preview. All six LC states, charge signs, current labels/arrowheads, two translated quarter-period headings and both spring states are visible in the complete composition.

Spring panels are reflowed side by side under their explicit first/second quarter headings. Group b remains distinct from group a; the physical shared equilibrium concept and opposite-side displacement are preserved.
At 640px fixed media width, minimum text is 16px. At the 331px viewport the SVG remains 640px, minimum text remains 16px, and scrollLeft=309 equals maxScroll=309.
The right-end mobile image exposes the last LC states and the compressed spring/x_m marker. Headings cut at the left viewport edge are ordinary scroll-end occlusion, not source-canvas clipping.

Broken equilibrium references and solid position extensions/vertical markers are visually distinct. No spring guide falsely acquires an arrowhead. The v_m and x_m vector accents are separate valid SVG paths.
No missing objects, black raster, overlapping labels or clipped full-canvas geometry was observed. Original collision/display checks pass and remain hash-bound to unchanged geometry.
Visible labels are English or mathematical symbols. No source Chinese/Cyrillic inscriptions, Soviet decoration, flags, handwriting or historical scan texture are retained.
All visible paint is semantic CSS-variable paint or context-stroke inherited by the current arrowhead from semantic ink. Hidden JSXGraph construction colors do not appear.

Uniform coil/spring geometry, modern whitespace, mechanical-panel reflow and repeated quarter headings for the reflow are justified presentation additions, not claims about the original source layout.

facts: Six closed LC circuits are arranged in two rows of three, each capacitor left and inductor right.
The first row is labelled First quarter-period; the second row is labelled Second quarter-period.
Top-left state: positive upper plate q_m and negative lower plate -q_m; no current arrow.
Top-middle state: reduced positive upper q and negative lower -q; current i arrow points DOWN beside the coil.
Top-right state: uncharged capacitor; I_m arrow points DOWN beside the coil.
Bottom-left state repeats the uncharged capacitor and DOWN I_m arrow as the start of the second quarter.
Bottom-middle state: negative upper -q and positive lower q; current i arrow still points DOWN beside the coil.
Bottom-right state: negative upper -q_m and positive lower q_m; no current arrow.
Charge marks change sign between rows; the current does not reverse within the depicted half-period.
The two quarter-period rows together depict HALF a period, not a full period.
Upper spring hangs vertically from a fixed hatched support, carrying one mass at the horizontal dash-dot equilibrium line.
The source label is vector v with subscript m, NOT v_x.
The short right-pointing mark above v is vector notation; it is not a horizontal mass-motion arrow.
No separate vertical motion arrow is visible in this source spring panel.
Equilibrium is labelled beneath the dashed guide.
Lower spring hangs from a second fixed support and carries a mass ABOVE its dash-dot equilibrium guide.
The spring is shorter/compressed relative to its equilibrium state.
A solid horizontal guide from the mass center and a vertical dimension mark to the lower equilibrium guide denote displacement magnitude x_m.
The label is x_m, not velocity; this extremum has zero speed by the physical spring analogy.
Solid measurement guides and dashed equilibrium guides have distinct meanings.
Both source spring panels belong to group b; neither can be omitted.
